description: Random bytes stored next to each hash, so equal passwords get different hashes and precomputed (rainbow) tables are useless.
A deliberately slow, tunable hash for passwords: PBKDF2, bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2id.
The cost parameter (iterations, rounds, memory). Raised over time as hardware gets faster.
Learning a secret from how long a comparison takes. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` always compares every byte.
An extra secret kept outside the database (an env var or KMS), mixed into every hash; useless to an attacker who only stole the database.
When a stored hash uses an old algorithm or cost, replace it after a successful login, the only time the plaintext is available.
